stem: One mole of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally at $300$ K from $2$ L to $20$ L. Find the work done on the gas. Take $R=2$ cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For reversible isothermal expansion, work on the gas is $W=-nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)=-600\ln 10\,\text{cal}\approx-1.38\,\text{kcal}$.

working:
$$w_{\mathrm{rev}}=-2.303nRT\log\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$$
$$=-2.303(1)(2)(300)\log(10)=-1381.8\ \text{cal}=-1.38\ \text{kcal}$$

Independent check: For reversible isothermal expansion, work on the gas is $W=-nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)=-600\ln 10\,\text{cal}\approx-1.38\,\text{kcal}$.
solution:
For a reversible isothermal expansion, work done on the gas is
$$w=-nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)=-600\ln(10)\ \text{cal}\approx-1.38\ \text{kcal}$$
